Since 2026-08-12 the PLATE verdicts are also re-read here against the built film, so a plate a reviewer rejected for an identifiable face can no longer reach the door by being rendered first -- but that too is the reviewer's free text, and a plate nobody looked at carefully passes it exactly as easily as one they did.

factual_support.detector: verify_onscreen_text (burned on-screen figures vs grade-A claims) + check_script_craft (forbidden-claim pass over the script) + check_packaging_claims (title/thumbnail/description vs this episode's own script, captions and ledgers)
factual_support.honest_limit: verify_onscreen_text SKIPS on this episode -- there is no claims.v*.json in 01_research, so it reports ok=true without measuring anything. check_script_craft compares the SCRIPT against the FACTS ledger by literal substring, so a paraphrase evades it. episode_spec.forbidden_claims (10 declared) is read by no gate that can refuse. Narration is compared against no claim ledger anywhere on the ship path. The TITLE, THUMBNAIL TEXT and DESCRIPTION are now read against this episode's own record by check_packaging_claims (2026-08-12, after two false titles cleared every mechanical rule), and it blocks -- but it matches words, stems and numbers only: it cannot judge tone or implication, it passes a title whose words are all in a script that is itself wrong, and a paraphrase the film states in other words reads as UNVERIFIED. A green from it is not a substitute for reading the title against the film.

plate_review.honest_limit: the plate verdicts for this episode ARE re-read against the built film (0 rejected and 0 unresolved plate(s) found in cuts, 0 blocking). IT NEVER LOOKS AT A PICTURE -- check_plate_verdicts.py says so in its own docstring, and this reads its file, not the plates. It proves a verdict exists, that it is bound to the bytes on disk, and that no plate a reviewer rejected or left unresolved was cut into the film. Whether the plates a reviewer ACCEPTED are actually right is a judgement nothing on the ship path re-checks, and a careless review passes this exactly as easily as a careful one. The class is read from the reviewer's own reason text by substring, so a reason worded in new words falls to unclassified and blocks rather than being guessed.
